text:
Alice Chen: Heads up — noticed a big jump in p99 for /v2/generate on the latency dashboard after yesterday's routing-policy rollout
Mateo Lopez: Which dashboard view? console per-endpoint rollup or raw telemetry?
Alice Chen: Console -> Endpoint breakdown (p50/p95/p99). p99 went from ~120ms to ~430ms for a 3hr window starting 02:15 UTC
Priya Singh: Hmm. Any change in sample counts? low-sample p99s can be noisy
Alice Chen: Sample count for that endpoint dropped ~60% in the same window (see screenshot link). p50 stable, p95 nudged up a bit
Dan Robinson: Routing-policy v3 routed more traffic to low-latency region but also introduced fallback to small-quant models; could be skewed by a tiny subset of requests hitting a different probe path
deploy-bot: deploy success: routing-policy v3 — canary -> promoted at 2024-06-15T02:12:04Z :white_check_mark:
eng-sre-bot: alert triggered: endpoint /v2/generate p99 > 300ms (3m) — investigation recommended
Mateo Lopez: Quick diagnostic query I ran: ```SELECT tdigest_percentile(0.5,0.95,0.99) AS p FROM latency_rollups WHERE endpoint='/v2/generate' AND ts BETWEEN X AND Y GROUP BY minute``` — the raw rollups show p99 spike aligns with a 10x reduction in sample weight
Priya Singh: That suggests aggregation/rollup sampling changed. We have two possibilities: (1) routing changed the client mix so fewer samples reached the telemetry sidecar, or (2) the rollup pipeline applied heavier sampling for that route after we bumped route weights
Kendra (UX): From a dashboard UX perspective we should surface sample counts next to percentiles and add a low-sample warning badge. People keep treating p99 as gospel when the counts are tiny
Dan Robinson: Agreed on the badge. Ops question: can we compute exact p99 at query-time for just this endpoint window? cost/latency tradeoff?
Mateo Lopez: Exact at query-time is expensive at scale. Options: (A) show sample_count + CI (e.g., Wilson/bootstrapped) and a gray out when count < N, (B) compute on-demand for selected windows (button: "compute exact") that spins a short job, (C) reduce sampling for critical endpoints in rollups
Alice Chen: Prefer B + C: quick on-demand exact for debugging and fix rollup config for high-traffic endpoints to keep stable sample rates
Priya Singh: We also need to check ingestion tags — if route tag was lost during the rollout, rollups could have dropped samples into the generic bucket 
Kendra (UX): Small mock: show p50/p95/p99, then a tiny metric: "samples: 42 (last 5m)" and an info icon with: "If samples < 100, percentile may be unstable. Run exact compute."
Dan Robinson: I'll open a telemetry ticket to: 1) audit rollup sampling by route since 02:00 UTC, 2) add a temporary low-sample badge, 3) expose on-demand exact compute (backend task).
Alice Chen: Thanks — tagging @Mateo to help with the audit query and @Kendra for UI text/placement.
Mateo Lopez: On it. I captured the raw payloads and will paste example logs in the ticket.
Priya Singh: If this is indeed a route-tagging regression, we should roll back routing-policy v3 for the affected customer cohort until fixed
Dan Robinson: Agreed. I'll coordinate with SRE to throttle promotion and open a rollback plan if the audit points to tag loss
Alice Chen: Great. For the short term I'll add a dashboard note to avoid confused on-call escalations. :memo:
Kendra (UX): Will sketch the badge and the "compute exact" button in Figma, share link here when ready
eng-sre-bot: incident-note: created issue #5981 (telemetry: route-sample-audit) assigned to Dan Robinson
Alice Chen: Closing loop — thanks team. We'll reconvene after the audit results. :thumbsup:
